Definition: as if from ξέω (properly, to smooth; by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher):--pot.
BiblicalUsage: When the Pharisees came from the market, except they wash, they eat not, and many other things there be which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, and brasen vessels.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the vessel exposes the heart: the measure was made for holding water, and the Pharisees made it a measure of holiness, and Jesus answered that cleanness is not poured from a cup.
